name: GMFlow
plain: GMFlow (2022; the flow models of UniMatch, 2023): optical flow as one global matching step between Transformer-enhanced features of both images; variants add a second matching scale and refinement steps. MIT code; the authors' weights carry no separate licence.
summary: GMFlow (Xu, Zhang, Cai, Rezatofighi & Tao 2022) in its UniMatch release (Xu et al. 2023): optical flow as global matching. A CNN gives features at 1/8 resolution, a Transformer with self- and cross-attention (shifted windows) makes the two images' features aware of each other, the flow is the expected position of the best match over the whole image, and a self-attention layer spreads it into occluded areas. `scale2` variants repeat this at 1/4 resolution with local matching; `regrefine6` variants add 6 RAFT-like local refinements.

papers.title: GMFlow: Learning Optical Flow via Global Matching
Unifying Flow, Stereo and Depth Estimation

official.reason: The authors' unimatch repository (the successor of their GMFlow code) carries the GMFlow models together with the regrefine models in one codebase.

no_kernels_reason: none of the existing kernels fits (window attention with one head, global softmax matching), and no new kernel was written for it
limitations: No custom kernels backend is implemented.
TensorRT builds at 1080x1920 fail for scale2 variants with a Myelin CHECK(is_const()) error on RTX 5060 Ti; scale1 variants build.
task_io: Input: two RGB images (consecutive frames). Output: per-pixel motion from the first to the second (dx, dy in pixels).
